implementation_notes: Kotlin's Boolean is a distinct type: conditions require it, 0 and 1 are not Boolean values and cannot be assigned to one, and there are no implicit conversions or user-defined conversion operators. A domain type is never testable by itself, so expose `fun isEmpty(): Boolean` and test with `if (q.isEmpty())`. When two boolean-valued predicates must not be mixed up, wrap the flag in a value class (`@JvmInline value class IsEmpty(val value: Boolean)`) so the call site has to name which flag it is instead of using a bare truth test.
pitfalls: `Boolean?` is not usable as a condition: use `== true`, `?: false` or `?.let` - a nullable flag from Java interop or from `Map.get` turns a test into a nullability question.
Java interop boxes booleans into java.lang.Boolean, and generics erase to Object, so a `List<Boolean>` holds wrappers and unboxing a null throws.
Value classes erase to their underlying type at runtime, so the nominal flag distinction is compile-time only and disappears in Java-facing APIs.
